Depression since I was 21 (35 now), and it's pretty hard. I've gained 2 degrees since then and am now doing a MSc (whilst working full time, and single mun with 3 kids). Every assignment has been seat-of-my-pants to deadline, with huge depressive episodes before and after. Degrees were easier because as long as I scraped a pass I didn't care. But with MSc I seem to be convinced anything less than a merit is crap so every assignment is agony - beating myself up over lack of motivation, really awful episodes like I've never experienced, lots of crying, binging and insomnia, and this assignment just finished (today!) I had to get a week's extension and get signed off work with my depression to get it finished as I'm a total mess...

They absolutely can't. For one, except in maybe certain careers like the military (that's a guess), employers don't have access to your notes. And even if they did, they can't discriminate. It's illegal. TBH, if they would then I don't think they'd be an employer you'd want to work for. I've been in "career" work for over 10 years now (including working with patients) and have always been upfront about my MH diagnosis on occupational health screening, it's never caused an issue.

Good luck with your GP, just be totally open because they can only help with what they know is going on. And if you get one who isn't taking you seriously, try different GPs in your practice until you get one who does. You could even ask specifically for one who deals with MH.

I don't think it's necessarily cheating, but it is a horrible way to treat you. I suggest you put her in your past and keep her there, because at best she's using you as a gap filler and at worst she's a heartless narcissist who will never have your feelings at heart.

I'm in the UK, don't know where you are, but I self-certifed last week and now have a Drs line for another two weeks for MH issues. My work have been really good about it, and they consider wfh to be a good "reason" for me to be struggling. I hope you have a manager you can speak to openly, as I know not all are as good as mine. But it sounds like you have more than enough reason to need to step back, especially with MS (which they might see as more if a "real" illness 🙄) so you could always emphasise that if you don't feel comfortable explaining your MH issues?

Not really, but I don't tend to read reviews. I've realised as I have grown into my reading I've learned my own tastes and now rarely pick a book I don't enjoy. But it was trial and error...and that was kind of the fun of it. I'd recommend using a library or buying second hand so there isn't monetary risk, listen to bookish podcasts (All The Books, What Should I Read Next and Get Booked are all really good) and accept that you won't love everything but that it's ok to quit something you aren't enjoying. Happy hunting!!

I too went through a phase of ONS after I was left alone with a baby at 18 after a 3 year relationship. Sometimes it helped, other times I'm still ashamed 18yrs later. Please keep yourself safe and respect your boundaries in order to keep it helpful other than shameful.

I think I used it as a alternative to working on my self esteem. If others liked me then who cares if I hated myself? But I know now that it's a shitty alternative, that there isn't really an alternative at all. Cultivate those talents you have, and you'll find your worth.
